gate_rules._why_these_pages: The eight surfaces where this brand's real proof has to appear: the homepage, the About and team pages (10 named clinicians with dated credentials — wedge M§1.2), the reviews page (the 506-review Birdeye record), the smile gallery (the one absent category that matters), the locations hub (the seven-office footprint — wedge M§1.6), and the two money pages the paid traffic lands on.
gate_rules._KNOWN_LIMITATION_needs_owner_decision: These rules are recorded for correctness, but they CANNOT currently be satisfied. verify-selling-assets-surfaced.mjs (client-site-build/scripts) implements required_one_of_proof as a hard-coded if/else over exactly three MediMarketing keys — solv_scans, results_dashboards, fcp_proof. Any other category name falls through every branch without pushing to proofHits, so the check errors with 'no hard proof category surfaced' no matter what a dental brand configures. Setting the list to [] does not help either: [] is truthy, so the default is not substituted, the loop simply does not run, and the same error fires. The only configuration that avoids a false block is proof_pages:[] — i.e. disabling the gate for this brand — which was NOT done here, because silently disabling a proof gate is worse than a visible, escalated block.
gate_rules._current_blast_radius: NONE TODAY. verify-selling-assets-surfaced.mjs is a DEAD gate: it is registered in no settings.json anywhere under .claude (re-verified 2026-07-31, zero matches; independently recorded in memory-template/seed-notes/feedback_selling_asset_gates.md as of 2026-06-22, and listed as DEAD in Code/client-website-builder/_design/_BUILD-FLOW-REORDER.md:75). It never fires, so neither this limitation nor the findManifest defect below can block the radiantsmiles build. Both become live the moment the gate is re-wired.
gate_rules._findManifest_reads_the_PREP_tree: Second defect in the same script. findManifest() walks up from the page for <dir>/_spec/selling-asset-manifest.json, then falls back to mapping client-sites/<brand>/ onto client-site-prep/<brand>/_spec/. Neither branch looks in _handoff/. So a re-wired gate would validate against the UNSEALED prep copy of C9 rather than the checksummed handoff copy — and doing so would itself violate HANDOFF-PREP-TO-BUILD.md §6 (PATH-EXCLUSION, decision D-B: the build reads binding inputs only from its own _handoff/, the single permitted exception being verify-handoff-current hashing four decision files). Mitigation in force meanwhile: the prep and _handoff copies of this file are kept byte-identical, so the wrong-source read is currently harmless.
gate_rules._owner_decision_required: Patch verify-selling-assets-surfaced.mjs to (a) honour brand-defined proof categories in required_one_of_proof instead of the three hard-coded MediMarketing keys, and (b) resolve the manifest from _handoff/ first, per §6. Both are edits to a SHARED skill asset used by every client including medimarketing, so they are not being made unilaterally (.claude/rules/04-code-modification.md). Same bucket as the gen-fact-registry.mjs must_convey guard.

ALL OF THAT WAS FALSE and is reversed here. Coverage is 10 of 10. The three 'missing' portraits were on disk the whole time: IMG_9391-1-2.jpg (1130x1177), IMG_4337.jpg (827x1191) and IMG_1387-1-scaled.jpg (2560x2438) — all three magic-byte verified as JPEG on 2026-08-03, all three md5-distinct from each other and from every other file in the 372-file pool (no duplicate group). THE DEFECT WAS THE INSTRUMENT, NOT THE DATA: the absence was asserted on a case-insensitive FILENAME search of assets/ for 'quizon', 'andrade', 'schaudt'. This practice stores its newer portraits under camera-generated names, so that search was structurally incapable of returning a hit and its null result carried no information whatsoever. The correct pairing was recovered from STRUCTURE and confirmed by TWO independent sources: (1) site-snapshot/meet-the-doctors.html, where each Elementor image-box binds exactly one figure image to one title inside a single elementor-image-box-wrapper — a rule that reproduces all seven independently-known pairs exactly (Ruiz, Miranda, Dang-Roberts, Torres, Subramani, Lavado, Landaverde, whose files already carry their own names), which is what licenses trusting it on the three camera-named ones; and (2) each clinician's own dedicated snapshot page, which carries the same image stem as their roster card. GENERAL LESSON, and it is the fourth instance on this spec: a search that cannot express the thing being searched for produces a null result that is not evidence. Absence must be established by an instrument capable of detecting presence.

financing_marks.detail: FOUR partners, FOUR real image files, but they are four DIFFERENT kinds of thing and only one is a clean logo. Verified 2026-07-31 by opening every file and reading the raw / markup in site-snapshot/. (1) CARE CREDIT — www.carecredit.com_sites_pc_image_carecredit_button_applypay_prequal_350x213_bluegreen_v1.jpg, 19,421 B JPEG. NOT first-party: the live pages hot-link it straight from https://www.carecredit.com/sites/pc/image/... and it exists on disk only because the P0.0 crawler followed that third-party URL. It is a CareCredit-supplied promotional BUTTON — card art plus 'Special financing options available*', 'See if you prequalify / Apply / Pay' and a 'Get Started' CTA — not a bare logo. Link target is an affiliate-coded URL (/go/279XQC/?dtc=DS7X&sitecode=CCCAPDS7X). (2) CHERRY — radiantsmilesnv.com_wp-content_uploads_2024_04_cherry.png, 6,268 B PNG, first-party hosted. A promo banner reading 'Cherry PAYMENT PLANS' over 'QUALIFY FOR UP TO $10,000 IN 60 SECONDS' — the dollar figure and the 60-second claim are Cherry's terms baked into the pixels, so it cannot be shipped as a neutral logo. A 300x158 derivative (cherry-300x158.png) also exists. (3) LENDING CLUB — radiantsmilesnv.com_wp-content_uploads_2024_04_LC-300x104-1.webp, 9,288 B WEBP, first-party hosted. The ONLY clean standalone wordmark of the four. (4) SUNBIT — radiantsmilesnv.com_wp-content_uploads_2024_04_Dntl_FB-Post_1080x1080-1.png, 575,436 B PNG, first-party hosted, wrapped in on 9 pages. NO file on disk and no markup attribute anywhere contains the string 'sunbit' in a FILENAME; the mark lives INSIDE this generically-named 1080x1080 social-post creative, which carries the 'Powered by sunbit' logo lockup plus 'Smile now, Pay-over-time.', 'Over 85% get approved' and 'Loans are made by TAB Bank.' All four appear on the same 9 pages (payment-plans, patient-information, and the 7 location pages).
financing_marks.caveat: ⚠FLAG — third-party trademarks, rights unconfirmed. Critically, the 0% interest / no down payment / no annual fee terms are the LENDERS' terms subject to approval, and the live site presents them as the practice's own with no disclosure. Any use must attribute. THREE FURTHER CONSTRAINTS, each verified on disk 2026-07-31 and each one a reason the build cannot simply drop these four in as a logo row: (a) NO STANDALONE SUNBIT LOGO EXISTS. Sunbit's mark is only available embedded in a lender-terms creative that also asserts 'Over 85% get approved' and 'Loans are made by TAB Bank' — shipping it ships those claims too. If the build wants a plain Sunbit mark it is ⚠OWNER, or name Sunbit in text only. (b) THE CARE CREDIT ASSET IS HOT-LINKED FROM CARECREDIT.COM, not served first-party. Reusing the on-disk copy re-hosts a third party's promotional button; reusing the live markup keeps a runtime dependency on carecredit.com. Either way it is a rights question, not just a file question. (c) TWO OF THE FOUR (Cherry, Sunbit) HAVE LENDER TERMS BAKED INTO THE IMAGE, so they cannot be used as neutral marks and the disclosure obligation is not dischargeable by adjacent body copy alone. Only Lending Club is a clean wordmark.
financing_marks._CORRECTED_2026_07_31_count_CHALLENGED_A: HISTORY, PRESERVED. An independent audit pass on 2026-07-31 reported this category as OVERSTATED — that count:4 should be 3, that visual-direction.md:76's '4 financing partner marks' was wrong, and that 'Sunbit appears as TEXT only'. Its evidence was two greps: `ls assets | grep -ic sunbit` = 0, and `` tags referencing sunbit across site-snapshot/ = 0. BOTH GREPS RE-RAN TRUE. THE CONCLUSION DRAWN FROM THEM IS FALSE, and count:4 is UPHELD unchanged. Both greps are NAME-based: they prove only that no filename and no img attribute contains the literal string 'sunbit'. They cannot see a mark that is filed under a name carrying no brand string. Re-derived by reading the raw markup instead of grepping for the brand: every financing block contains WRAPPING an , on 9 pages. That PNG was then OPENED, not inferred from its filename, and it is unambiguously a Sunbit asset — the 'Powered by sunbit' logo lockup, 'Smile now, Pay-over-time.', 'Over 85% get approved', 'Loans are made by TAB Bank.' So a Sunbit mark DOES exist on disk, first-party hosted, and 'text only' is wrong. This is the same failure class as the earlier existsSync-instead-of-magic-bytes retraction (see proof_categories.credentials._RETRACTION_2026_07_31) and the & entity miss: a cheap string test standing in for opening the artifact. WHAT THE AUDIT DID GET RIGHT, and what is corrected here: the old assets[] was a single vague string, 'assets/ (Care Credit, Cherry, Sunbit, Lending Club logo files)', which enumerated no path, implied four first-party 'logo files', and was therefore uncheckable — it is replaced above with the four real paths plus a per-partner detail of what each file actually is. Corroborating counts, re-derived 2026-07-31: client-rules.json pricing.financing_partners lists exactly these 4; a search for any fifth lender (Alphaeon, GreenSky, Proceed, Affirm, Klarna, Afterpay, LendingPoint, iCare, Springstone, Wells Fargo Health) across site-snapshot/ returned ZERO; and the only external financing hrefs in the whole snapshot are sunbit.com, carecredit.com, pay.withcherry.com and lendingclub.com.
